sentences.text:
Neeraj Choubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:611
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani
On The 10th Of January, 2025

Misc. Criminal Case No. 55325 of 2024
 Neeraj Choubey
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:

Shri Ayush Saxena - learned counsel for the applicant.
 Shri Samar Ghuriya - learned Public Prosecutor for the  respondent/State.
ORDER 1.

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS (439 of Cr.P.C.)
for grant of bail relating to Crime No.379/2024 registered at Police Station Dabra District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of I.P.C.
2.
The allegation levelled against the applicant is of defrauding a sum of Rs.6,70,000/- from the complainant.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the present applicant that applicant is in custody since 16.9.2024.

After dismissal of his first bail application vide order dated 22.10.2024, charge sheet has been filed on 26.12.2024; therefore, in the change circumstances, this subsequent bail application has been filed.
As per prosecution story, complainant has transferred a sum of Rs.1,70,000/- in the bank account of complainant.
So far NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:611 2 MCRC-55325-2024 as Rs. 5,00,000/- is concerned the receipt of that amount has been given by co-accused Raghuvendra Sharma.
As regards the criminal history, one more case under Section 420 of I.P.C. has been registered against the applicant which is related to minor offence.
He is ready to deposit Rs.1,70,000/- under protest.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application and prayed to dismiss the bail application.

6. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on depositing Rs.1,70,000/-
before the trial Court and furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
In case, if he is found involved in the offence of same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
